transcript: Bees are one of the most important partners for humanity. They fly from flower to flower, carrying pollen. Without this work, many crops do not bear fruit. One third of the food grown in the world depends on pollinators such as bees. The richness of our table is supported by the work of small bees. But in recent years the number of bees has been decreasing around the world. The causes are complex pesticides, the destruction of habitat, climate change, Parasites, especially serious are pesticides Containing neonicotinoids But these chemicals interfere with the nervous system of bees And cause them to lose their sense of direction Bees that cannot return to the hive are isolated and eventually die Why the EU has banned the use of these pesticides? Other countries are gradually strengthening restrictions But there is also strong opposition to regulation Farmers worry that yields may fall without effective alternatives What must be weighed is agricultural productivity against environmental protection Citizens can also act Plant plenty of flowers in the garden And provide bees with nectar Buy honey from local beekeepers Try gardening without pesticides Bees function within the network of the ecosystem If they disappear, many organisms will be affected Throughout the food chain in the end The food security of humanity itself comes under threat A small being supports a great world To protect bees is to protect our own future
